title: Kinetic-Ballooning and Resistive X-Point Dynamics in Quasicontinuous Exhaust Tokamak Plasmas
abstract: We investigate quasicoherent modes (QCMs) and their interaction with scrape-off-layer (SOL) plasma blobs (filaments) in the type-I-ELM-free quasicontinuous exhaust (QCE) regime, extending the analysis in [K. Zhang et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 055102 (2026)]. Two-fluid electromagnetic turbulence simulations are compared for two self-consistent turbulence states with different separatrix densities. In both cases, a separatrix-spanning QCM resides within the radial-electric-field well, whereas blobs are observed only in the case with higher separatrix density. The QCM exhibits similar kinetic-ballooning-mode (KBM) signatures in both cases, with modest differences in coherence and harmonic content. The primary difference is the presence of an additional resistive X-point mode (RXM), which emerges as the near-X-point collisionality increases. The coexistence of the KBM and RXM shifts the potential--density cross-phase from its KBM-like value toward the interchange value in the SOL, allowing QCM perturbations to be ejected as blobs. These intermittent blobs account for over half of the net radial $E\times B$ transport in the far SOL. Neither QCM onset nor blob ejection requires an increase in upstream collisionality. The results distinguish the KBM-dominated mechanism that regulates the pedestal from the RXM-assisted blob-launching mechanism that enables intermittent SOL exhaust.
